name: Reclaim.ai
summary: Auto-schedules tasks, habits and meetings around your stated priorities. Google Calendar-first, so Outlook-heavy teams are out, and the free tier is limited.
best_for: Google Calendar teams that want AI to auto-schedule tasks, habits and meetings around their priorities
skip_if: you run hosted or on-premise Exchange, which Reclaim's help centre lists as unsupported, or you don't overbook your calendar: the auto-scheduling has little to optimize
honest_knock: The magic only works on a calendar it can write to. Google Calendar was first, but Microsoft 365, Outlook.com and Exchange-backed accounts are supported too (reclaim.ai/integrations/outlook-calendar, read 15 September 2026); Reclaim's own help centre still lists hosted and on-premise Exchange as unsupported. The free tier is quite limited. A genuine time-saver for the right setup, useless for the wrong one.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per seat a month billed yearly ($12 monthly)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on reclaim.ai/pricing, USD, and in our own test that day; earlier: re-verified 2026-10-03) Four levels, and the page keeps both billing terms in the markup rather than recomputing them. Lite is free forever for a single user. Billed yearly the seats are Starter $10, Business $15 and Enterprise $22 per seat a month; billed monthly Starter is $12 and Business $18, and the monthly column marks Enterprise 'Unavailable on monthly plans'. Seats are capped by tier rather than open: 1 user on Lite, up to 10 on Starter, up to 100 on Business and over 100 on Enterprise, with the AI-agent allowance per seat stepping 5, 10, 100 and unlimited beside them. Calendar Syncs are counted per plan: 1 on Lite, 3 on Starter and unlimited from Business. In our test on 18 November 2026 the app showed Unlimited Calendar Syncs on Starter, and on Lite the 'Add a sync' button carried a STARTER label, so check the count in your own account. The Attendee Unit packs are no longer shown: on 18 November 2026 the page showed neither the AU packs nor the '20% off with code MEETINGS' banner. Both are still in the page code but hidden, so we no longer count either as part of the price. Our October reading listed AU packs from $8 for 3 on Starter, for attendees without a paid seat in Smart Meetings of 3 or more. The page now lists four discounts you apply for: Student 50% for 12 months (students, educators and faculty), Nonprofit 20% for 3 years, Startup 20% for 3 years, and Switching Providers 20% for 6 months when you move from Clockwise, Motion or Calendly. The site now carries a Dropbox Reclaim logo (alt text 'Reclaim.ai from Dropbox').

schema_offer.description: Starter per seat, per month, billed month-to-month. From our pricing notes: “Billed yearly the seats are Starter $10, Business $15 and Enterprise $22 per seat a month; billed monthly Starter is $12 and Business $18” Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-18.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Reclaim (now Dropbox Reclaim) in the existing Lite our account after a calendar was linked with only the calendar scopes: a habit appeared in the calendar within seconds and moved by itself within about 3 seconds when a busy appointment came in, and back when it was removed, but it is set to Free by default so others can book over it. Two tasks with a deadline and a duration got no block of their own; Tasks is marked Beta and shows them only as a suggestion inside a habit, and priority or an earlier deadline only changed the order of the list. The primary calendar cannot be unlinked, only by deleting the account. The app lists Unlimited Calendar Syncs for Starter where the public page says 3, Lite promises 1 Calendar Sync while Add a sync has a STARTER label, and the in-app yearly prices are in euro. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing Reclaim our account (social login, no sign-up during the test), on the Lite plan, with the interface in English. Three earlier attempts (08:51 to about 09:30) stopped before a calendar was linked: the onboarding needs a calendar, the Continue button stays grey without one, and a Google consent has to come from we ourselves. The scope list in the Google link was read from the link: only calendar events and calendar list (read and write), plus name and mail address, no Gmail, Drive, Contacts or Tasks. The calendar of a test mailbox of we were then linked at about 09:33 on our approval, and the real test ran from 09:33 to 09:47. The brand is now Dropbox Reclaim (reclaim.ai from Dropbox), the dossier name is Reclaim.ai and the review is on AIBM (b2b/reclaim-ai-review); the handson folder is reclaim. Onboarding: Continue, then Turn on my assistant or Maybe later (Maybe later chosen), then the About you page (Finish worked without any choice), then the planner at about 09:35, about 2 minutes and 3 clicks after the start. A banner offered premium features free for 30 days plus 30% off the first year, with a countdown; it was not clicked. Settings and the billing page show Lite as the current plan, and no trial was active. The planner of the week and the next week held no appointment before the test, only two onboarding tasks of Reclaim in the task list. Core action, tasks: two tasks were made with Create, Task (Draft test report, 2 hrs, due 20 November; Review test notes, 1 hr, due 20 November) with the message Task created. You'll find it in your Reclaim Tasks. Neither task got a block in the calendar, also not after a reload and about 3 minutes of waiting. They appear only in the Tasks side panel (marked Beta) under Now: Free time, with Mark Done and Start Task; the task menu has Edit, Priority, Start timer, Log work and Delete, and no option to schedule. Setting the priority of one task to Critical moved it to the top of the list within about 3 seconds and moving the deadline of the other to an earlier day changed only the order of the list; the calendar did not change. Tasks only show as a suggestion inside a habit block (Task Suggestions, Assign Tasks, a saved search); in Preview Mode that could not be set (Cannot change the saved search while previewing). Core action, habit: Create, Habit opens the Agent library; Custom Work Habit was chosen and in Preview Mode three blocks of 10 to 11am (Wednesday to Friday) were shown within about 2 seconds. It was renamed Test focus block (Every weekday, 10 to 11:00am, Shallow Work, Free, Default visibility, Default reminders, 30 mins minimum, Working Hours, Skip when busy, Reclaim Smart Time Defense enabled). After Apply changes at about 09:38 (Your changes have been applied and will sync shortly.) the block was in the calendar of the day within seconds, and the next weeks showed blocks Monday to Friday 10 to 11 as dashed, provisional blocks. A busy test appointment (Test conflict block, 10 to 11am; the date field did not take 19 November, so it landed on 18 November) pushed the habit block to 11am to 12pm within about 3 seconds at 09:39, and when the appointment was deleted the block jumped back to 10 to 11 within a few seconds. The habit does what Reclaim promises, quickly and by itself, but it is set to Free by default, so other people can still book over it. Plans, read up to the payment step: the billing page (Select a plan, Based on your usage the Starter plan looks just right for you, Get your first 30 days free. Cancel at any time.) was only looked at, nothing was clicked. Yearly toggle, currency EUR, 1 user: Lite Free (Current plan; 1 user team, 5 Agents/seat, Limited LLM usage, 1 Scheduling Link, Essentials integrations, 1 week scheduling range, 1 Calendar Sync, Limited MCP access); Starter EUR 8 per seat/month (up to 10 seats, 10 Agents/seat, 3 Scheduling Links, Unlimited integrations, 8 week scheduling range, Unlimited Calendar Syncs, Full MCP access, Proactive Assistant); Business EUR 15 (up to 100 seats, 100 Agents/seat, 12 week scheduling range, Team OOO Calendars, Delegated Access); Enterprise EUR 22 with Contact us (SSO and SCIM user provisioning). The public pricing page (images 02 and 03) shows dollars: yearly $10, $15 and $22 per seat/month, monthly $12 and $18, and Enterprise Unavailable on monthly plans. Deviations from the dossier and the public page: (a) the app lists Unlimited Calendar Syncs for Starter, the public page says 3. (b) Lite promises 1 Calendar Sync on both pages, but in Settings the Add a sync and New sync buttons carry a STARTER label. (c) The in-app yearly prices are in euro (8, 15 and 22) against $10, $15 and $22 on the public page, with no conversion rate shown; the euro and dollar prices are not compared. (d) The Attendee Unit packs and the 20% off code MEETINGS of the dossier are gone from the public page and the app; new offers are Student 50% (12 months), Nonprofit 20% (3 years), Startup 20% (3 years) and Switching Providers 20% (6 months), plus the 30 days free offer in the banner. (e) The brand is now Dropbox Reclaim. (f) The Lite limit of 1 week scheduling range was not seen: habit blocks stood two weeks ahead, though dashed. (g) Enterprise is not available on monthly plans. The price fields of our pages are not touched. Checkout: NOT reached. No plan, trial or Upgrade now button was clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: Settings, Calendars shows for the main account only the menu item Delete account, and the switch of the primary calendar says Primary calendar on main account cannot be disconnected, so the calendar cannot be unlinked without deleting the account; Delete account was NOT clicked. Calendar access reads 5 scopes granted, 2 partially granted and 2 missing (granted: Identity and sign-in, Read calendar events, Create and edit events, Calendar access, Settings; partial: Availability and Out of office sync; not granted: People suggestions and Tasks); Grant access to all was not clicked. Reclaim keeps read and write access to the calendar until the access is withdrawn in the permissions of the Google account, which the tester did not do. There is no paid plan to cancel. Not tested: the Focus Time agent, Buffers, Smart Meetings, Scheduling Links (the page was only looked at), Calendar Sync, Outlook calendars, integrations (Asana, ClickUp, Jira, Linear, Todoist, Zoom, Slack), Reclaim Chat, the paid plans and the 30 days trial, and the groups of managers with shared time off and teams on Microsoft 365 calendars. Clean up: both test tasks and the two onboarding tasks were deleted (the task list is empty). Removing the habit (Remove Agent) has a tick box Also remove future events that is OFF by default; without the tick the blocks stay in the calendar, and the block of the day stayed as an ordinary repeating appointment (Every weekday, until Nov 18, 2026), which was then deleted with All events; the test appointment was deleted too. At 09:44 the planner of three weeks held no test, habit or focus entry. The five default Essentials agents were switched off. The calendar link could not be removed. The account stays on Lite. The tab was closed.
exit_test.awkward: The onboarding cannot be finished without a linked calendar, and the primary calendar cannot be unlinked again; the only way out in the app is Delete account. Tasks get no calendar block of their own and are only a suggestion inside a habit (Tasks is marked Beta). A new habit is set to Free, so others can book over it. Removing a habit leaves the future blocks in the calendar unless you tick Also remove future events, which is off by default. Starter shows Unlimited Calendar Syncs in the app but 3 on the public page, and Add a sync has a STARTER label although Lite promises 1 Calendar Sync.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We read the Reclaim plans and tested the planner in the existing Lite our account on 18 November 2026, with a test calendar linked through calendar scopes only. A custom habit showed up in the calendar within about 2 seconds and moved to a free slot about 3 seconds after we added a clashing event, then moved back when we removed it. The habit defaults to Free, so others can book over it. Two tasks with a duration and a deadline got no calendar block of their own: Tasks is marked Beta and only suggests them inside a habit. We bought no plan.
findings: Text we checked: "Unlimited Calendar Syncs". What we saw: The in-app plan card of Starter lists Unlimited Calendar Syncs, while the public pricing page says 3 Calendar Syncs for Starter. Neither number was exercised.

Text we checked: "1 Calendar Sync". What we saw: Lite promises 1 Calendar Sync on both pricing pages, but in Settings, Calendars the Add a sync and New sync buttons carry a STARTER label, and the Calendar Syncs box says No syncs are set up. Whether a Lite user can make the one sync was not tried.

Text we checked: "Task created. You'll find it in your Reclaim Tasks". What we saw: Two tasks with a duration and a deadline were made and found in the task list, but neither got a block in the calendar, also not after a reload and about 3 minutes. Priority Critical and an earlier deadline changed only the list order. Tasks is marked Beta and shows tasks only as a suggestion inside a habit. The dossier says Reclaim auto-schedules tasks.

Text we checked: "Skip when busy". What we saw: The habit block appeared in the calendar within seconds, moved from 10 to 11am to 11am to 12pm within about 3 seconds when a busy test appointment was put in the same hour, and jumped back within a few seconds when the appointment was deleted.

Text we checked: "code MEETINGS". What we saw: The dossier mentions Attendee Unit packs and the 20% off code MEETINGS. The public page no longer shows them and the app showed no packs. New offers are Student 50% (12 months), Nonprofit 20% (3 years), Startup 20% (3 years) and Switching Providers 20% (6 months), and a 30 days free banner.
not_tested: Focus Time agent, Buffers, Smart Meetings, Scheduling Links, Calendar Sync, Outlook calendars and the integrations.
Reclaim Chat and the Lite limit of 1 week scheduling range.
Sign-up, which was done earlier by us.
Checkout, the paid plans and the 30 days trial, and Delete account.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 09:33 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

claim_checks.observed: The in-app plan card of Starter lists Unlimited Calendar Syncs, while the public pricing page says 3 Calendar Syncs for Starter. Neither number was exercised.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The in-app plan card against the public pricing page on the same day; no Calendar Sync was made, so the limit itself was not tried.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A buyer who needs many syncs may get more on Starter than the public page says, or the page is out of date.

claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The pricing page line against the label on the buttons in Settings; no sync was started.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A free user may be unable to use the one sync that the plan lists.

claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier wording on tasks against two tasks on one Lite account, in one session of about 15 minutes; the Starter and Business plans were not used.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A buyer who expects tasks to get time in the calendar by themselves has to attach them to a habit first.

claim_checks.observed: The habit block appeared in the calendar within seconds, moved from 10 to 11am to 11am to 12pm within about 3 seconds when a busy test appointment was put in the same hour, and jumped back within a few seconds when the appointment was deleted.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier wording on habits against one habit and one conflicting appointment; larger calendars and many habits were not tried.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Habit blocks do defend their time and move around busy slots by themselves, as promised.

claim_checks.claim: Shallow Work, Free, Default visibility, Default reminders
claim_checks.observed: The new habit is set to Free by default, so other people can book over the block, and the block stays visible as a normal event.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: A default setting of one habit; no stored claim about the default exists in the dossier or on the public page.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Someone who wants the time to be really protected has to change this setting for each habit.

claim_checks.claim: Also remove future events for: Test focus block
claim_checks.observed: Removing a habit has a tick box to also remove future events, which is OFF by default. Without it the blocks stay in the calendar, and the block of the day stayed as an ordinary repeating appointment until it was deleted by hand.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: A removal dialog default seen once; no stored claim about the removal exists.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Leaving a habit behind leaves appointments in your calendar unless you tick the box.

claim_checks.claim: Primary calendar on main account cannot be disconnected
claim_checks.observed: The switch of the primary calendar of the main account is locked with this message, and the account has only the menu item Delete account. The calendar could not be unlinked again, so Reclaim keeps its read and write access until it is withdrawn in the permissions of the Google account.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: An app message against a dossier remark that Reclaim needs a calendar it can write to; no earlier claim about unlinking exists. Delete account was not clicked.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A buyer who tries Reclaim cannot go back to an unlinked calendar without deleting the account or withdrawing access at Google.

claim_checks.observed: Lite lists a 1 week scheduling range on both pricing pages. In the planner the habit blocks stood two weeks ahead, though dashed (provisional), so the limit was not seen.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: A plan limit line against dashed blocks in a planner that may be showing a preview; the blocks were not checked in the calendar itself.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: It is unclear how far ahead a Lite user can really plan.

claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: Euro prices in the app against dollar prices on the public page, which are two currencies on two pages; no exchange rate or tax was applied.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The price depends on currency, toggle and page; the amount to compare is only clear at the checkout.

claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier text against the public pricing page of 18 November and the app; the discounts were not applied.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The old code and the packs cannot be counted on; the new discounts may lower the price for some buyers.

claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier brand against the public page header and the app logo; no terms were read.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The vendor is part of Dropbox now; terms, data handling and prices may follow Dropbox.

claim_checks.claim: Get your first 30 days free. Cancel at any time.
claim_checks.observed: The billing page offers the first 30 days free and says to cancel at any time; no plan, trial or Upgrade now button was clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen. The price of Starter is EUR 8 per seat a month on this page.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the billing page and the public pricing page were read without clicking a plan button
claim_checks.comparability: The billing page offer against a checkout that was not reached; no stored cost rule was compared.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The final amount with tax and the way to cancel a trial are not confirmed.

Starter shows Unlimited Calendar Syncs in the app but 3 on the public page, and Add a sync has a STARTER label although Lite promises 1 Calendar Sync.
